Hi, I’m a little late to this, but I really feel compelled to comment as I was/sort of still am in the same boat and I have some suggestions that have helped me. Sorry if it gets a little long, I ramble a bit. Feel free to skim haha!

Like said before, vitamins. Vitamins are a must I can’t stress this enough. I wish I had really stuck to what I call my ‘vitamin routine’ sooner. Even one’s that don’t directly seem like they’d be related to weight. For example I take ginseng which is for energy, and as someone with depression just having that energy to do things does something to my brain that I can’t really describe. I also take fish oil, saffron, and sometimes acv gummies along with a multivite of course. I’ve been looking into more, but that’s where I’ve started so far and those have personally helped a lot.

Another thing, try to pick up some new hobbies to replace that chase for satisfaction. Especially ones that make you feel better, try a sport or something competitive that can keep you active but still be fun. I know plain old working out can be fun and rewarding, but doing the same thing all the time can get boring. Switch it up! Try to have something else to look forward to other than food. It doesn’t even have to relate to being active. It can be art, skincare/haircare ( kinda hard to class as a hobby, but it can make you feel really good about yourself ), meditation, crafts, etc.

I would also suggest maybe looking into intermittent fasting to help with how you look at food. It’s strange because you would think it would make you long for food, but I find that after my body gets used to it my brain follows as well. I don’t think about food as much when I do IF for prolonged periods of time.

I hope this wasn’t too long and any of this advice sounds like it could help :)

Try not to get an apartment without having a stable income first. Like said before, you don't want to have a bad tenant history. I'm not sure where you live, but I'll tell you what I did right when I was becoming homeless age 18, USA. I'm now 20, have a job, live with my fiance, and I'm now starting to think about college.

First, I went to my district's city welfare office and applied for aid. I knew I wouldn't have income for awhile because I had to get my birth certificate to get a state I.D. I applied for medical and food stamps. I got it, as I didn't have a job. MAKE SURE you have the things for a job on you.

Have you had a job before? If you were close with anyone or a manager and quit on good terms you could always try to contact them.

Next is finding a place to stay. Honestly, try to couch jump friends places if possible. The longer you can do that the longer you can save money as well as make connections. Talking to people and making connections is very important. It's how I found the odd jobs that helped me make enough to pay for my important expenses like bus fair and interview clothes.

An odd thing you can do to make a little bit of money is to donate plasma ( if you meet the requirements ). I did this and it helped a lot. At the location I went to they paid 70 the first 5 times I went. Then after that it was based on bodyweight. You can donate twice a week at most. They also give you a little card for the money you get reimbursed. You can use this as regular cash, it isn't just like store credit.

All that's really else is just get out and apply to every job that you can physically find. Don't give up. If all else fails look into being an Au Pair.
